fact: The 'ear of wheat' in the Maiden's hand — a close pair whose dance helped reveal precession.
bio: Spica (Alpha Virginis) is a hot blue pair of stars about 250 light-years away, so close together that they orbit in just four days and are distorted into egg shapes by mutual gravity. Their combined light makes Spica the brightest star in Virgo.
cultural: Its Latin name means 'ear of grain', the sheaf of wheat held by Virgo the harvest maiden. Observations of Spica let Hipparchus detect the slow precession of the equinoxes over two thousand years ago.
